title: Week 1 Advanced: Accounts (Windows)
readme:
You administer this computer. A security review found account problems. Fix them without removing people the company needs.

Authorized users: alice, bob, carol, dave, frank, and the service account svc_wsman.
Authorized administrators: you, and alice.

Not every problem shows in Settings > Accounts. Check the full local user list (lusrmgr.msc, or Get-LocalUser / net user), membership of every privileged group — not just Administrators — whether the machine logs on automatically, and how passwords are stored. Company policy: only authorized people, only authorized admins, no automatic logon, and passwords never stored in a recoverable form.

This computer also provides a WinRM remote-management service that administrators rely on; it has been left stopped. Bring it back into service, make the service account svc_wsman a least-privileged Remote Management user rather than an administrator, and make sure no unauthorized account (such as wsmanguest) can manage the machine remotely.

There are 13 problems, 20 points each. Removing an authorized user is a penalty.
setup:
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
# Baseline for Week 1 (Accounts) Advanced. Forces each problem into place so a hardened VM still
# starts with all of them. Standard account-hardening checklist, harder to spot than the Basic set.
function New-Pw { (-join ((48..57)+(65..90)+(97..122) | Get-Random -Count 14 | ForEach-Object { [char]$_ })) + 'Aa1!' }
foreach ($u in 'alice','bob','carol','dave','frank','mallory') {
    $pw = ConvertTo-SecureString (New-Pw) -AsPlainText -Force
    if (Get-LocalUser -Name $u -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { Set-LocalUser -Name $u -Password $pw }
    else { New-LocalUser -Name $u -Password $pw -PasswordNeverExpires | Out-Null }
    Add-LocalGroupMember -SID 'S-1-5-32-545' -Member $u -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue   # Users
}
# alice is the authorized administrator
Add-LocalGroupMember -SID 'S-1-5-32-544' -Member 'alice' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
# 1) mallory is an obvious unauthorized user. 2) a second account that does not show in the normal
#    user list (its name ends with $, so "net user" and the sign-in screen skip it).
if (-not (Get-LocalUser -Name 'sysadmin$' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
    # net user prompts (Y/N) for passwords longer than 14 chars and fails non-interactively, so use 14
    $hp = (-join ((48..57)+(65..90)+(97..122) | Get-Random -Count 10 | ForEach-Object { [char]$_ })) + 'Aa1!'
    net user "sysadmin$" $hp /add | Out-Null
}
Add-LocalGroupMember -SID 'S-1-5-32-544' -Member 'sysadmin$' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue  # Administrators
# 3) bob should be a normal user. 4) carol is in a privileged group other than Administrators.
Add-LocalGroupMember -SID 'S-1-5-32-544' -Member 'bob' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue         # Administrators
Add-LocalGroupMember -SID 'S-1-5-32-551' -Member 'carol' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue        # Backup Operators
# 5) dave does not need remote desktop
Add-LocalGroupMember -SID 'S-1-5-32-555' -Member 'dave' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue          # Remote Desktop Users
# 6) Guest is on. 7) the built-in Administrator is on.
Get-LocalUser | Where-Object { $_.SID.Value -like '*-501' } | Enable-LocalUser
Get-LocalUser | Where-Object { $_.SID.Value -like '*-500' } | Enable-LocalUser
# 8) the machine logs on automatically, with the password stored in the registry
$w = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon'
Set-ItemProperty -Path $w -Name AutoAdminLogon -Value '1'
Set-ItemProperty -Path $w -Name DefaultUserName -Value 'bob'
Set-ItemProperty -Path $w -Name DefaultPassword -Value 'Spring2024!'   # demo value, not a real secret
# 9) bob's password never expires
Set-LocalUser -Name 'bob' -PasswordNeverExpires $true
# 10) passwords are stored with reversible encryption
$inf = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'sp_setup.inf'
@"
[Unicode]
Unicode=yes
[System Access]
ClearTextPassword = 1
[Version]
signature="`$CHICAGO`$"
"@ | Set-Content -Path $inf -Encoding Unicode
secedit /configure /db (Join-Path $env:TEMP 'sp.sdb') /cfg $inf /areas SECURITYPOLICY /quiet

# --- Remote-management service (WinRM): left stopped, with an over-privileged service account and
#     an unauthorized remote user. The student must bring it back up, least-privilege svc_wsman, and
#     remove the unauthorized remote access. ---
function New-Pw2 { (-join ((48..57)+(65..90)+(97..122) | Get-Random -Count 10 | ForEach-Object { [char]$_ })) + 'Aa1!' }
foreach ($u in 'svc_wsman','wsmanguest') {
    if (-not (Get-LocalUser -Name $u -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
        New-LocalUser -Name $u -Password (ConvertTo-SecureString (New-Pw2) -AsPlainText -Force) -PasswordNeverExpires | Out-Null
    }
    Add-LocalGroupMember -SID 'S-1-5-32-545' -Member $u -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue   # Users
}
Add-LocalGroupMember -SID 'S-1-5-32-544' -Member 'svc_wsman' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue    # Administrators (the vuln)
Add-LocalGroupMember -SID 'S-1-5-32-580' -Member 'svc_wsman' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue    # Remote Management Users
Add-LocalGroupMember -SID 'S-1-5-32-580' -Member 'wsmanguest' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue   # unauthorized remote access
Stop-Service -Name WinRM -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Set-Service -Name WinRM -StartupType Disabled -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

checks.message: Removed the account that is hidden from the user list
bob is no longer an administrator
carol is no longer a Backup Operator
dave is no longer in Remote Desktop Users

pass.cmd:
$g = Get-LocalUser | Where-Object { $_.SID.Value -like '*-501' }
if ($g -and -not $g.Enabled) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 }

checks.message: The built-in Administrator account is disabled

pass.cmd:
$a = Get-LocalUser | Where-Object { $_.SID.Value -like '*-500' }
if ($a -and -not $a.Enabled) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 }

checks.message: Automatic logon is turned off and no password is stored for it

pass.cmd:
$w = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon'
$a = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $w -Name AutoAdminLogon -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).AutoAdminLogon
$p = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $w -Name DefaultPassword -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).DefaultPassword
if (($a -eq $null -or $a -eq '0') -and [string]::IsNullOrEmpty($p)) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 }

checks.message: bob's password is allowed to expire
Passwords are not stored with reversible encryption
The remote management service (WinRM) is running and responds

pass.cmd: try { Test-WSMan -ComputerName localhost -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null; exit 0 } catch { exit 1 }

checks.message: The WinRM service account svc_wsman is not an administrator
No unauthorized account can manage the machine remotely
